answer.rationale: The two measured deficits are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage move is one that attacks the actual funnel regression rather than the competitor's price move. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifting first-week activation) point at the same mechanism from two independent records, and memory_91 (activation messaging) is a compatible follow-on rather than a substitute; I chose onboarding over messaging because onboarding sits upstream and its lift was reported on both completion and adoption, not engagement alone. I want memory_86 verified because it is the memory I am actually acting on and I should read its original record rather than the consolidated summary — in particular whether 'self-serve accounts' includes the segment now under competitive pressure and whether the lift persisted past the measurement window. I want memory_73 verified because it is the memory most likely to pull the team toward promotional_pricing this week and it is the least trustworthy on its face: it is compressed to the point of telegraphy, reports signup +31% against a smaller rev +18% (consistent with discount-driven volume of lower-value accounts), and its '12 reporting wks' window plus the note that segment definition was unchanged are exactly the details that decide whether that revenue was durable or borrowed. Discounting into a competitor's entry-price move also risks resetting price expectations and importing churn-prone, price-shopping accounts — a direct threat to the objective of sustainable qualified revenue, so I am flagging that downstream risk rather than treating the +18% as settled. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) and referral incentives (memory_57) are both credible but address pipeline quality and expansion, not the regression; referrals in particular amplify whatever the current funnel produces, which is currently degraded. Standard experiment scale with a holdout and a qualified-revenue readout, not just completion rate; if verification shows memory_86's lift was window-limited or segment-specific, I would fall back to activation_messaging at a guarded scale rather than to discounting.
